items.summary: AstraZeneca is paying insitro $40 million upfront to find novel drug targets for liver and heart diseases using artificial intelligence.

items.title: Rebranded Galapagos finally finds buyer for unwanted cell therapy pipeline
items.summary: Lakefront Biotherapeutics—the new name for Belgium’s Galapagos Therapeutics—has found a buyer for its unwanted cell therapy pipeline.

items.title: Iambic goes public with $150M IPO to accelerate clinical development of oncology pipeline
items.summary: Iambic Therapeutics’ IPO came in dead on target, bringing in $150 million for the AI biotech to fuel the clinical development of its oncology pipeline.

items.title: Vanda pauses social anxiety program after ex-Novartis asset flunks phase 3 study
items.summary: A phase 3 trial of Vanda Pharmaceuticals’ social anxiety disorder drug candidate has missed its primary endpoint, prompting the company to put the program on hold.

items.title: Why OMass’ $310M series C marks ‘fantastic milestone’ on journey to become ‘Britain’s Big Biotech’
items.summary: When Fierce last caught up with OMass Therapeutics’ CEO Ros Deegan, it was hard not to be impressed by the company’s ambition.

items.title: IQVIA, Veeva expand on existing partnership for speedier clinical trials
items.summary: Clinical research giant IQVIA and cloud system provider Veeva Systems have expanded their partnership to further increase trial speed and efficiency.

items.title: Merck KGaA spinout iOnctura touts PI3K delta inhibitor in metastatic eye cancer
items.summary: iOnctura’s PI3K delta inhibitor shows promise in phase 1 study in patients with mostly pre-treated metastatic melanoma.

items.title: Verastem CEO claims RAS drug has 'set a new benchmark' for tricky cancer in early readout
items.summary: Verastem Oncology's decision to refocus its R&D efforts on its KRAS inhibitor appears to be paying off, at least based on initial data from a phase 1/2 trial.

items.title: Deep-pocketed Verdiva axes GLP-1 switching trial over ‘market evolution’
items.summary: Verdiva Bio has scrapped a phase 2 trial of its once-weekly oral GLP-1 drug candidate VRB-101, pulling the plug the year after launching with $410 million.

items.title: Biomea posts phase 1 data to pitch oral GLP-1 to potential partners, but investors appear unconvinced
items.summary: Biomea Fusion has shared phase 1 data on its oral GLP-1 prospect, shedding light on a small molecule designed to balance efficacy and gastrointestinal tolerability. Management hailed the data as a launchpad for talks with potential partners, but investors drove down the share price of the cash-strapped biotech.

items.title: Vir CEO sees ‘opportunity to do more deals’ after striking $1.9B Gilead pact for dual-masked TCEs
items.summary: Looking to expand its oncology portfolio, Gilead has tapped Vir Biotechnology’s masked T-cell engager tech in a potential $1.9 billion biobucks deal.

items.title: GSK to lay off over 1,200 roles in Belgium as cost-saving program picks up steam
items.summary: Up to 1,217 GSK employees in Belgium are at risk of losing their jobs as the Big Pharma rolls out its global cost-saving plans.

items.title: Zealand inks $1.2B Generate pact to add multispecific proteins to obesity pipeline
items.summary: Zealand Pharma is paying Generate Biomedicines $30 million upfront to collaborate on multispecific drug candidates for metabolic diseases. Milestones could bring the total value of the deal above $1 billion.

items.title: Agilent spends $240M upfront to buy digital pathology specialist Proscia
items.summary: Agilent Technologies is buying up the digital pathology software company Proscia in an all-cash transaction valued at $240 million with an additional $30 million on the cards for future performance milestones.

items.title: Stryker pens deal with CMR Surgical to advance robotic-assisted surgery
items.summary: Stryker will funnel around $400 million (£300 million) in a “strategic” investment in CMR Surgical and its robot surgery tech.

items.title: WCG unveils AI-powered solution to accelerate clinical trial kickoffs
items.summary: WCG, a clinical trials solutions provider, is launching an AI-powered program dubbed Activation Intelligence to help study sites accelerate clinical trial start-up.

items.title: Insulet’s Omnipod Discover platform sees full market release in US
items.summary: Insulet Corporation has announced the U.S. full market release of Omnipod Discover, a web-based data platform designed for Omnipod 5.

items.title: BioNTech’s mRNA cancer vaccine fails phase 3 test, significantly denting analysts’ confidence
items.summary: A phase 2/3 clinical trial of BioNTech’s mRNA cancer immunotherapy BNT113 has missed one of its dual primary endpoints. But with immature overall survival data offering a path to redemption, the German biotech is continuing to track patients in the metastatic head and neck cancer study.

items.title: Biotech builder Paragon imports Apogee's top brass after AbbVie buyout
items.summary: It’s been a busy morning for Paragon Labs. In addition to bringing over much of the leadership team from AbbVie-acquired Apogee Therapeutics, Paragon has overseen a reverse merger to take its hypertension-focused spinout Velaris Therapeutics public.

items.title: Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker '26: OMass obtains $310M; Soufflé cooks up $135M
items.summary: The Fierce Biotech Fundraising Tracker records venture capital rounds of $50 million or more secured by biotechs.

items.title: Roche inks $1.2B deal with China's Rona to enter emerging ALK7 obesity race
items.summary: Roche has committed $100 million in upfront and near-term payments to license Rona Therapeutics’ ALK7 drug candidate, joining Alnylam, Arrowhead, GSK and Novo Nordisk in an emerging obesity niche.

items.title: Pfizer pens $500M Enodia pact to join Lilly in emerging protein degrader field
items.summary: Pfizer has followed Eli Lilly into the Sec61 space, inking a $500 million deal with Enodia Therapeutics days after its Big Pharma peer formed an $870 million pact with Gate Bioscience.

items.title: Drugmakers, PhRMA seek to intervene in hospitals' 340B rebate challenge
items.summary: The American Hospital Association and others have launched a legal rematch with the federal government over the second iteration of a pilot program swapping out safety-net hospitals’ upfront drug discounts for after-the-fact rebates.

items.title: Kindeva lands $226M defense contract to supply nerve agent antidote in US
items.summary: Kindeva's Meridian was awarded a $226 million defense contract to supply the U.S. military with its self-injected nerve agent antidote and bolster national defense against chemical threats.

items.title: Par Health recalls 22 lots of IV blood thinner, its 3rd US product pull in a month
items.summary: Par Health issued a recall of 22 lots of the intravenous anticoagulant argatroban, the latest in a string of recent recalls related to IV-bag contamination risk.

items.title: With new Omvoh analyses, Lilly argues 'higher bar' for IBD treatment is within reach
items.summary: In the fiercely competitive inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) market, Eli Lilly is making the case for its antibody Omvoh as a holistic solution for patients living with ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease—and one that could offer relief after other biologic drugs have failed, too.

items.title: Gilead puts a timely spotlight on HIV prevention in Latino communities with 'Ahorita Mismo' campaign
items.summary: Gilead's “Ahorita Mismo (Right Now!)” stars two popular Latino creators in a call-in podcast-themed spot looking to spark conversations around HIV prevention.

items.title: Isotope supplier NorthStar continues rise with partnership to tee up China radiopharmaceutical filings
items.summary: As the momentum continues to pick up at NorthStar Medical Technologies, the radioisotope producer is strengthening ties in China, in a move that helps put its actinium-225 supplies on the map for local radiopharmaceutical filings.

items.title: Compass puts treatment-resistant depression on the map with first awareness day
items.summary: Compass Pathways has partnered with mental health organizations on the first-ever awareness day for treatment-resistant depression.

items.title: FDA clears ImmunityBio’s Anktiva expansion in bladder cancer after regulatory whiplash
items.summary: To expand Anktiva’s label, the FDA adopted a new approach to how it evaluates treatments for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC. The new regulatory path essentially allowed ImmunityBio to bypass an expensive randomized phase 3 trial that competitor Johnson & Johnson is currently forced to grind through.

items.title: Ultragenyx makes swift $413M return on FDA review vouchers after summer of gene therapy nods
items.summary: Hot off a pair of key FDA approvals this summer, rare disease specialist Ultragenyx has wasted little time cashing in on the priority review vouchers it earned from the green lights.

items.title: United lands 'clear-cut win' as Liquidia agrees to $380M settlement in Tyvaso patent infringement saga
items.summary: With a years-long patent dispute between the two drugmakers finally put to bed—complete with a hefty settlement payout—United Therapeutics has clinched what one analyst calls a “clear-cut win” over lung disease rival Liquidia Technologies.

items.title: Galderma bulks up dermatology portfolio with $1.5B acquisition of Zo Skin Health
items.summary: Expanding its presence in dermatology, Cetaphil maker Galderma has agreed to acquire professional skincare shop Zo Skin Health for $1.5 billion.

items.title: AbbVie marks calendar for ‘Time For Treks’ in National Park Foundation, CLL Society partnership
items.summary: AbbVie's “Time For Treks” brings the chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) community together for an outdoor gathering at Cabrillo National Monument, San Diego, on Oct. 17.

items.title: Regulatory tracker: Pierre Fabre's Ebvallo takes 3rd run at FDA approval
items.summary: In this tracker, Fierce Pharma is recording the regulatory progress of in-market products, including expansions into key geographies and new indications. Some of these updates may not meet the bar for standalone stories, but we think they are still worth mentioning.

items.title: FTC seeks sanctions against Martin Shkreli over alleged pharma ban violations
items.summary: The FTC alleges that “Pharma Bro” Martin Shkreli flagrantly traded pharmaceutical stocks on social media for three years, violating his lifetime ban from the industry.

items.title: NantWorks' Soon-Shiong puts chips behind manufacturing disruptors in new rounds for Prolific Machines, Multiply Labs
items.summary: With demand for advanced manufacturing solutions mounting across the industry, the moment is ripe to capitalize on investor interest and build out toward a potential production paradigm shift.

items.title: Sanofi dodges EU fine over alleged disparagement of CSL flu vaccine
items.summary: Sanofi has avoided a European Union fine after antitrust regulators accepted its commitments to address the alleged disparagement of CSL Seqirus’ rival flu vaccine.

items.title: Syndax shares fall 17% after calling it quits on Niktimvo fibrosis program
items.summary: Syndax and Incyte are cutting their idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis program short after a phase 2 trial failed to meet its primary endpoint. The drugmakers plan to refocus on expanding the study drug Niktimvo's label for its original indication, graft-versus-host disease.

items.title: J&J’s new pharma chief expects Icotyde’s psoriasis launch momentum to repeat across indications
items.summary: As Johnson & Johnson rode out 2026’s third quarter, leveraging its pharmaceutical segment to navigate medtech headwinds, much of the company’s near-term excitement has turned to IL-23 pill Icotyde.

items.title: BARDA awards Kaléo $96M contract to deploy auto-injector for chemical threat preparedness
items.summary: Drug-device maker Kaléo has secured a federal contract worth $96.1 million to bolster U.S. biodefense.

items.title: UCB fashions ‘Wear It Out’ project with empowering t-shirts, community for inflammatory disease patients
items.summary: The t-shirts let those with hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), plaque psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis (PsA) reclaim clothes they may avoid due to their disease.

items.title: ARPA-H program manager talks 'first-shoring' philosophy behind $125M RNA manufacturing network challenge
items.summary: Rather than another instance of on-shoring enthusiasm, ARPA-H’s personalized RNA drug production network project should be viewed as more akin to a “first-shoring program,” said John Schiel, Ph.D., program manager for GIVE at ARPA-H.

items.title: Galderma sculpts new narrative around menopausal skin changes to fill awareness gap
items.summary: One in two women is unaware that hormonal fluctuations during perimenopause and menopause can affect their skin, a Galderma survey found.

items.title: Mirum on its way to 3rd rare liver indication for Livmarli
items.summary: Livmarli significantly improved severe itching caused by rare liver diseases. With the phase 3 win in hand, Mirum is looking for a third indication from the FDA early next year.

items.title: Bausch + Lomb names Appio interim CEO as Saunders hits the exit again
items.summary: Less than four years after returning to Bausch + Lomb to lead the eye health company following its split from Bausch Health, Brent Saunders is hitting the exit once again, as analysts call the transition a surprise.
